text:
jamie: Quick sync — customer asks keep coming for larger batch embeddings + richer response shape (per-item metadata, model tags). I sketched a proposal, want thoughts before I put in a PR.

rohit: lgtm high level. main tradeoffs: batching limits vs memory pressure on GPU workers, and format change vs backwards compatibility.

sophia: +1. Also need to decide which dims we officially support and how we label them in the response (e.g. "dims" vs "length").

jamie: Proposal summary:
- Add optional response_type="objects" (default: "arrays") so we don't break existing clients.
- Keep old arrays response: { embeddings: [[...],[...]], model: "..." }
- New objects response: { embeddings: [{ id, embedding, metadata?, model, dims }...] }
- Batch-size limits default 1024 items, hard cap 4096 for Dedicated; hosted default 512. We can map to worker memory and queueing.

rohit: Those caps seem reasonable. Implementation note: continuous-batching needs to know max_items_per_batch to control padding. We should expose a per-model batch_hint for runtime tuning.

alex: runtime can expose "batch_hint" as metadata in model catalog. We can also enforce per-request header "X-Req-Max-Items" to override up to tenant cap. But careful with Dedicated SLA.

jamie: launch criteria I propose:
- API shape stable behind response_type flag and documented.
- SDKs for python/js ship with both modes.
- Perf: P95 end-to-end (hosted) for batch=32 < 200ms, for batch=256 < 1.2s.
- Memory: worker OOM rate 0 in 50k requests stress test.
- E2E compat tests and one major customer integration (beta).

rohit: Add quality criterion: model mapping must have model_fingerprint in response so we can track regressions (embedding drift).

jamie: Good call. We'll include model_fingerprint (short hash) and model_name.

sophia: About dims: we should support 1536 and 768 first. Response uses integer "dims" field. Also include "vector_type" e.g. "float32" or "int8_q4" for quantized responses.

jamie: Agreed. For quantized we should only return quantized vectors to Dedicated/private unless customer opts in.

alex: Ops note: for quantized payloads we need a header "X-Embed-Format: q4_0" and we should record that in request logs for billing/metrics.

jamie: Example new response (objects):
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-large-1536",
  "model_fingerprint": "mfp_9a3f",
  "embeddings": [
    {
      "id": "input-0",
      "embedding": [0.001, -0.23, ...],
      "dims": 1536,
      "vector_type": "float32"
    },
    {
      "id": "input-1",
      "embedding": [0.12, 0.003, ...],
      "dims": 1536,
      "metadata": { "source": "upload-2026-02-14" }
    }
  ]
}
```

rohit: Nice. Two implementation questions: 1) maintain input order always? yes. 2) per-item errors (e.g. length too long) — return per-item error field and still return others?

jamie: Yes on both: maintain order and support per-item errors array with null embedding for failed items. That reduces roundtrips.

sophia: Tests: create sythetic cases with mixed success/failure and ensure SDK surfaces per-item error codes. Add a migration guide for users.

alex: infra: need metrics: batch_size histogram, vector_dims, response_type, quantized flag. Also add a rollout plan: beta opt-in via tenant flag for 4 weeks, collect feedback, then gradual rollout.

jamie: Action items:
- rohit: draft API changes + server PR (due 2/10)
- sophia: write model mapping + dims/quantization spec (due 2/12)
- alex: infra metrics + header handling + tenant flag (due 2/12)
- jamie: publish draft docs + SDK checklist (due 2/14)

rohit: I'll add unit + perf tests to the PR. One question: should we add a compact embedding binary transport (CBOR/msgpack) later?

sophia: Let's leave binary transport for v2; too risky for beta. Note it in backlog.

jamie: Sounds good. If no objections I'll open the RFC PR today and tag eng/ops/docs. Thanks all. :rocket:

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: No deploys scheduled. Remember to run integration tests against preview infra before canary.
